[[St. Louis, Missouri]] | awards = * [[FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] MVP ([[2010 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|2010]]) * SEC All-Freshman Team ([[2011–12 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|2011–12]]) * First-Team All-SEC (2011–12) }} '''Bradley Beal''' (born June 28, 1993) is an [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player. After his freshman season for the [[University of Florida]] [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Gators men's basketball team]], Beal announced he would enter the [[2012 NBA Draft]]. ==High school== Beal attended [[Chaminade College Preparatory School (Missouri)|Chaminade College Preparatory School]] in [[St. Louis, Missouri]]. He competed in the [[2010 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] for the USA, which won the championship with Beal averaging 18 points per game.{{cite web|title=FIBA.com-2010 FIBA U17 World Championship for Men Top Players|url=http://www.hamburg2010.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/10/fu17wc/men/statistics/p/eid/4718/sid/4718/tid/379/top-players.html}} During his senior year of high school, Beal averaged 32.5 points per game, 5.7 rebounds per game and 2.8 assists per game. At the end of Beal's senior season, he was named the 2011 [[Mr. Show-Me Basketball]] which recognized him as the top high school basketball player in the state of Missouri.{{cite web|title=Mr. and Miss Show-Me Basketball|url=http://www.mobca.org/ShowMeBasketball/default.html}} He was also named the 2011 [[Gatorade National Player of the Year]]. According to [[ESPNU]] recruits, Beal was the fourth ranked recruit and second ranked shooting guard and he was also the fourth ranked recruit according to [[Rivals.com]].{{cite web|title=Gator Men's Basketball Roster/Bios|url=http://www.gatorzone.com/basketball/men/bios.php?year=2011&player_id=39}} ==College career== On November 30, 2009, Beal committed to the University of Florida.{{cite web|title=Rivals.com-Brad Beal recruiting profile|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Brad-Beal-88579}} Beal accepted an [[athletic scholarship]] to attend the university, where he played for coach [[Billy Donovan]]'s [[Florida Gators men's basketball]] team during the [[2011–12 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2011–12]] season. In his first game at Florida, Beal started and recorded 14 points. Beal was named SEC Freshman of the Week on November 28, 2011. During the week of 11/21–11/28, Beal averaged 8.5 points, seven rebounds, two assists and 1.5 steals in two wins over [[Wright State]] and [[Jacksonville University|Jacksonville]].{{cite web|title=Beal Named SEC Freshman of the Week|url=http://www.gatorzone.com/story.php?id=21898|accessdate=29 November 2011}} Beal would go on to win five additional SEC Freshman of the Week honors and be named to the SEC All-Freshman Team and was a first-team All-SEC selection.{{cite web|title=Three Gators Earn Men's Basketball All-SEC Honors, Young Named Scholar-Athlete of the Year|url=http://www.gatorzone.com/story.php?id=22575|accessdate=6 March 2012}} Beal finished the season second on the team in scoring with 14.8 points per game. On April 13, 2012, Beal announced that he would forgo his sophomore season and enter the [[2012 NBA Draft|NBA Draft]].{{cite web|last=Harry|first=Chris|title=Bradley Beal Informs Gators of Intentions to Turn Pro|url=http://www.gatorzone.com/story.php?id=22903|accessdate=13 April 2012}} ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- |style="text-align:left;"|[[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2011–12]] |style="text-align:left;"|[[2011–12 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida Gators]] |37||37||34.2||.445||.339||.769||6.7||2.2||1.4||0.8||14.8 |} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * [http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/66909/bradley-beal ESPN.com- Bradley Beal recruiting profile] * [http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Brad-Beal-88579 Rivals.com- Bradley Beal recruiting profile] {{Gatorade National Basketball Player of the Year}} {{Persondata | NAME = Beal, Bradley | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = June 28, 1993 | PLACE OF BIRTH = | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Beal, Bradley}} [[Category:1993 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Missouri]] [[Category:Florida Gators men's basketball players]] [[Category:Gatorade National Basketball Player of the Year]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Parade High School All-Americans (boys' basketball)]] [[Category:People from St. Louis, Missouri]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[ru:Бил, Брэдли]]
